rgb: This indoor salon scene has a tiled floor, a brick fireplace structure on the right roughly 3 to 4 metres away, a black rolling cart directly to the fireplace’s left, and blue salon chairs and seating units in the left and upper-left background about 3 to 5 metres away. Roughly 0.4 to 0.6 metres directly ahead of and below the standing camera wearer, within arm’s reach, a person wearing a white jacket is seated facing forward and away from the wearer, with their head angled downward and their lower body cropped by the bottom edge of the frame. The wearer holds a black hairdryer and round brush around 0.3 to 0.5 metres from the viewpoint, immediately above and in contact with the seated person’s hair. In the upper-left background, approximately 3 to 4 metres away, a small child stands facing a blue manicure chair, while a seated adult is positioned just behind and left of the child, separated by about 0.5 to 1 metre. Both face generally rightward/away from the camera wearer and neither looks toward the viewpoint; in frames 2 through 4, the raised hairdryer and the wearer’s left arm partly block both of their heads. Over the five frames, the wearer’s left hand lifts the hairdryer higher into the upper-left foreground in frame 2, points it downward at the seated person’s hair in frames 3 and 4 as the right hand keeps the brush beneath it on the left side of the head, then moves the dryer slightly lower and leftward in frame 5. The room’s people and furnishings otherwise stay mostly still.
depth: The depth map depicts a salon-like indoor space in which the camera wearer’s raised left arm, right hand, hairdryer, and round brush are the brightest foreground elements, approximately 0.2–0.5 m away and within arm’s reach. They sit directly above and in front of a seated person’s head and upper torso, located about 0.5–0.8 m below the viewpoint. Beyond them across the tiled floor, roughly 3–5 m from the camera and 2.5–4 m behind the foreground person, dark-grey regions represent a standing child beside a blue salon chair/desk, a seated adult around 0.5–1 m to the child’s left, a black rolling cart on the right, and a brick fireplace structure farther right. Through the five frames, the wearer’s left arm and dryer move from the lower-left in frame 1 to a high overhead position in frame 2, before angling downward toward the right in frames 3–5 as the nozzle nears the top of the seated client’s head. They partly obscure the background child and seated adult in frames 2–4, while the client’s lower body and the wearer’s torso remain outside the view below the bottom edge. Relative to RGB alone, the depth image clearly distinguishes the planes of the dark dryer, its thin dangling cord, and the client’s dark hair, which otherwise visually blend, while also revealing the floor’s continuous receding slope. The map becomes unreliable in frames 3–5 where the nozzle and client’s hair combine at one uniform brightness, and in the upper-left background beyond 4 m, where furniture and the seated person collapse into almost indistinguishable black silhouettes.
segmentation: The segmentation map separates the scene into distinct regions, including the seated client in the lower-center foreground, 0.5–0.8 m away and facing away from the camera wearer while looking downward; the wearer’s raised left arm entering at the bottom-left, 0.2–0.4 m away; the black rolling cart in the upper-center at 2.5–3 m; and the distant child and seated adult in the upper-left at 3–4.5 m. Both background people face generally rightward/away from the wearer and are within arm’s reach of the blue salon furniture. Across all five frames, the foreground masks change as the wearer’s left arm and hairdryer swing overhead in frame 2, blocking the distant child, and then travel downward and rightward in frames 3–5. The seated client stays still underneath, and only the wearer’s hands, dryer, brush, and the client’s head fall within the wearer’s arm’s reach. Although the map produces crisp boundary contours around the wearer’s foreground arm and consistently follows the rolling cart, labeled ‘chair,’ at about 3 m in every frame, its semantic labels and temporal consistency are highly unreliable. In particular, frame 2 combines the wearer’s arm and dryer into one ‘person’ mask; frame 3 incorrectly labels the dryer and client’s head as ‘backpack’ and ‘laptop’; frame 4 omits the foreground client mask entirely; and frame 5 classifies the client’s head/dryer as a brown ‘person’ mask containing a tiny ‘cell phone’ at the bottom where the brush and right hand appear. The right-side brick fireplace, the blue chair at the bottom-left roughly 1.2 m away, and the distant background sofa also remain wholly unsegmented throughout.
pose: The pose map remains nearly empty throughout the sequence, finding only a magenta left-hand skeleton belonging to the camera wearer about 0.3–0.4 m away in the upper-left foreground of frames 3, 4, and 5, along with a deformed yellow body-and-torso polygon in the lower-center foreground of frame 4 at roughly 0.6 m. In frames 3 and 4, the magenta hand pose places the wrist on the left and the fingers reaching rightward and slightly upward while the hand grasps the hairdryer handle above the seated client. In frame 5, it moves lower and angles down toward the right as the wearer lowers the arm and rotates the dryer. Where detected, the keypoints clarify the precise positioning of the wearer’s thumb and curled fingers around the dryer grip better than the motion-blurred RGB imagery. Nevertheless, the map is very unreliable: it detects no body or hand skeletons at all in frames 1 and 2, never identifies the wearer’s right hand holding the brush along the bottom edge about 0.4–0.5 m away, and entirely misses both the distant standing child and seated adult at 3–4.5 m. Moreover, the yellow body skeleton appearing briefly in frame 4 falsely spans the hairdryer and the seated client’s head and shoulders without conveying any genuine anatomical orientation, so the facing directions and poses of all three other people in the room are left unrepresented.
